Comments: On 4/27/2026, the Department conducted an inspection at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. Present were Rosie Wise (DEP Environmental Trainee) and myself. This inspection follows up to IR 4168852, where violations were left outstanding due to no observable Act 9 sign and available Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. Also, at the time of this inspection, no response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. At the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. At the time of IR 3978494, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks.The following was observed during the inspection:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (photo 1). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection. However, they still lack compliant secondary containment to 78a.64(a), as is required at unconventional well sites (photos 4, 6, and 7). No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the gas well (photo 10). The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (photos 3 and 11). Outstanding violations issued against the operator's posted information are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team. The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (photos 9 and 12). A violation was issued in IR 4170358 for failure to remove equipment that is not necessary for production, in accordance with in accordance with OGA3216(C). The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (photos 5 and 12).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued in IR 4168852 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

MIA 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect well quarterly for Mechanical Integrity Assessment. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit annual report to the Department for Mechanical Integrity Assessments. APR 78.121(A) - Failure to submit annual production report. 78.121(B) - Failure to electronically submit Annual Production Report to the Department.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to Swn Prod Co Llc in Liberty Twp, Tioga County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-08-28 to Swn Prod Co Llc in Liberty Twp, Tioga county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Swn Prod Co Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-08-28
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 860200
Permit API: 117-22055
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-08-28
Comments: I inspected the site in response to a reported spill(Complaint ID#344679). I met Mike Deming of SWN when I arrived. He informed me that after washing and vaccing the liner yesterday, the liner and felt were placed in 4 rolloff containers that Waste Management had sent to the site without interior liners. In the process of loading the liner and felt into the containers, the loader compresses the material with the bucket; soapy water was then observed running out of the end of the rolloffs. Mike believes that the felt retained some rig wash solution (SDS forthcoming) and water, and that the compression of the material squeezed this mix out. He stated that the estimate of 2 barrels (84 gallons) was probably high, but that SWN was committed to an Act 2 cleanup process. The affected area appeared to be approximately 30' x 70'; puddled water on the pad in this area showed consistent conductance readings of 1.21-1.28 mS/cm. Two of the rolloffs were still on the pad with the swing gate end raised up on rig mats; while I was on location, a vac truck was used to suck the water out that had collected in the low end of the rolloffs. The north sed trap (.147 mS/cm) and the south sed trap (.441 mS/cm) appeared to be unaffected by the release. The rolloffs were removed and the free water on the pad was vacced while I was on site; a skid steer was scraping the area when I departed. Moody & Associates employees were directing the excavation with conductance meters, and Mike expects confirmation sampling to occur later today or early tomorrow. The site remediation will be referred to the Department's Environmental Cleanups Program. Violations noted.

Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of Spring Creek Road in July 2008. A spill was reported to the Department at 16:28 on April 1, 2019. The spill occurred when the brine tank overflowed. Oil was allowed to escape and contact the ground surface. The reported release amount was of approximately 30 gallons. Because the estimated spill volume was less than 1 bbl, a visual clean-up at this site was appropriate. A culvert under the access road has overtopped, allowing sediment to be carried into the stream in this HQ watershed. More work is needed to correct the E&S violations associated with this culvert. The violations can be closed when the site has been stabilized and all requested information has been received.

Report Details

Violation ID: 8230687
Permit API: 063-33033
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/24/2025
Comments: The Department received a complaint on 3/5/2025 that there were E and S issues with the access road for the Samual Serian 1 1470 well. On 3/10/2025, I conducted a complaint inspection of Diversified Production, LLC's Samuel Serian 1 1470 well (API 063-33033) in Grant Twp., Indiana County. During my inspection, I observed numerous areas of accelerated erosion. Violations were cited for the erosion and sedimentation issues with the access road. A Notice of Violation was sent on 3/20/2025, and Diversified sent a response on 3/28/2025. On 4/11/2025, Brian Shank (WQSS) and I met Heather Empfield, AJ Smith and John Stibrik at the access road for the Samual Serian 1 1470 well. We discussed different ideas to address the culvert and eroding access road. Today, Brian Shank, Samantha Lutz (Aquatic Biologist 2), Danielle Zimmerman (Environmental Engineer) and I met at the access road for the Samual Serian 1 1470 well. The Department recommends submitting a GP11 to replace the culvert and repair the access road. The existing 4 culvert pipes will need to be replaced with a single pipe. The outstanding violations from the 3/10/2025 complaint inspection will remain open.

Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/08/2026
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8277562
Permit API: 123-47222
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/08/2026
Comments: A discharge of production fluids is evident at the Loomis Lease tank battery. Elevated specific conductance in soils was observed beneath one of the stock tank's drain valves within the secondary containment area as well as throughout a swath of stressed and dead vegetation downslope of the Loomis Lease tank battery. Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) and I (Mat Haemer WQS-DEP) were present for this inspection.Evidence of a concentrated flow of fluids was observed just beyond the secondary containment diking. Bare soils outside of containment were observed to have been eroded in a manner consistent with the channelized flow of a large volume of fluid. The bottom of the eroded channel was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.Areas downslope of the tank battery where the flow of fluid was observed to widen (visible via the wide swath of stressed and dead vegetation) were observed to have elevated specific conductance in soils in excess of 5,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.The downslope path of the released fluid was then captured by a lease road ditch approximately 150 feet downslope of the tank battery. Observations of elevated specific conductance in soils within the road ditch continued to a culvert nearby to the Loomis Lease Loomis 3 OG well. Standing water at the outflow of this culvert was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 1,300 micro Siemens per centimeter. Elevated soil conductivity readings in excess of 1,000 micro Siemens per centimeter continued for approximately 100 feet from the outfall of the culvert.The total observed path of stressed/dead vegetation and elevated conductivity readings was approximately 750 feet in length and up to 30 feet in width. Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with receipts documenting the proper disposal of brine resulting from producing the Loomis Lease.

Comments: On 9/9/2024, I conducted an inspection at the Kentor Inc Well Pad following a produced fluid spill reported to the DEP Emergency Hotline by EQT on 9/6/2024 (CTS #383608). The spill was initially identified as staining on the ground that was discovered upon the removal of secondary containment for the Kentor 8H Well plugging operation. The spill was later updated to be greater than 5 gallons, but it was unclear the exact amount of produced fluid that was spilled onto the well pad.On site at the time of inspection was SPSI for spill remediation. SPSI indicated that they had remediated areas right of the plugged well, and a 30x60 foot area right of the plugged well was delineated by sandbags. SPSI stated that rain received on site on 9/6/2024 likely resulted in the produced fluid spill migrating out further across site. It was not clear at the time of inspection the cause of the spill nor how much produced fluid had spilled. A full spill delineation was not evident at the time of inspection. 2 rolloff boxes of impacted material were staged on site at the time of inspection, and SPSI was awaiting a third box to continue remediation.I spoke to Logan Dominick of EQT via phone call during my inspection who stated that the spill would likely be classified as an Act 2 Spill, and that the Kentor 8H Well was transferred to Leatherwood LLC to be plugged for mine-through.While on site I observed the following:-The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance and the access road appeared to be in generally good condition (Photos 1-3).-Aggregate staining as a result of produced fluid was evident immediately surrounding the left and right of the plugged well when entering the site. Aggregate was being excavated immediately around the plugged well at the time of inspection. I observed a range of conductivity readings in the stained aggregate surrounding the plugged well, varying from 2.18 mS/cm to 10.01 mS/cm. Standing fluid left of the plugged well appeared to have greater conductivity readings (Photos 4-12).-SPSI informed me while on site that they had discovered a soft spot in the aggregate on the well pad during initial remediation approximately 75-100 feet from the plugged well. Upon excavating this soft spot, produced fluid began filling up the hole. I observed conductivity readings of 10.01 mS/cm of the produced fluid standing within the hole, and the soil/aggregate read at 1859 us/cm (Photos 13-15).-Staining on the ground approximately 20 feet from the excavated hole with produced fluid within it resulted in normal conductivity measurements (Photo 16).-I observed conductivity readings of 5.65 mS/cm of standing fluid within the 30x60 ft spill delineation. Standing water located behind a black tarp at the edge of the delineated area demonstrated normal conductivity (Photos 17-21).-At the time of inspection, SPSI was excavating surficial aggregate/soil that was demonstrating overall conductivity readings of 4 mS/cm (Photos 22-23).-Standing fluid within a sump/trench dug near the left-side of the Kentor Well Site demonstrated normal conductivity (Photos 24-25).Violations of 91.34(A), 78a.57(a), 78a.54, and SWMA 301 are being issued for the spill. In addition, The Department is requesting Leatherwood LLC's Kentor 8H Well plugging secondary containment plan and the maintenance records associated with the secondary containment used in the plugging process.

Inspection Date: 9/09/2024
Comments: On 9/9/2024, I conducted an inspection at the Kentor Inc Well Pad following a produced fluid spill reported to the DEP Emergency Hotline by EQT on 9/6/2024 (CTS #383608). The spill was initially identified as staining on the ground that was discovered upon the removal of secondary containment for the Kentor 8H Well plugging operation. The spill was later updated to be greater than 5 gallons, but it was unclear the exact amount of produced fluid that was spilled onto the well pad.On site at the time of inspection was SPSI for spill remediation. SPSI indicated that they had remediated areas right of the plugged well, and a 30x60 foot area right of the plugged well was delineated by sandbags. SPSI stated that rain received on site on 9/6/2024 likely resulted in the produced fluid spill migrating out further across site. It was not clear at the time of inspection the cause of the spill nor how much produced fluid had spilled. A full spill delineation was not evident at the time of inspection. 2 rolloff boxes of impacted material were staged on site at the time of inspection, and SPSI was awaiting a third box to continue remediation.I spoke to Logan Dominick of EQT via phone call during my inspection who stated that the spill would likely be classified as an Act 2 Spill, and that the Kentor 8H Well was transferred to Leatherwood LLC to be plugged for mine-through.While on site I observed the following:-The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance and the access road appeared to be in generally good condition (Photos 1-3).-Aggregate staining as a result of produced fluid was evident immediately surrounding the left and right of the plugged well when entering the site. Aggregate was being excavated immediately around the plugged well at the time of inspection. I observed a range of conductivity readings in the stained aggregate surrounding the plugged well, varying from 2.18 mS/cm to 10.01 mS/cm. Standing fluid left of the plugged well appeared to have greater conductivity readings (Photos 4-12).-SPSI informed me while on site that they had discovered a soft spot in the aggregate on the well pad during initial remediation approximately 75-100 feet from the plugged well. Upon excavating this soft spot, produced fluid began filling up the hole. I observed conductivity readings of 10.01 mS/cm of the produced fluid standing within the hole, and the soil/aggregate read at 1859 us/cm (Photos 13-15).-Staining on the ground approximately 20 feet from the excavated hole with produced fluid within it resulted in normal conductivity measurements (Photo 16).-I observed conductivity readings of 5.65 mS/cm of standing fluid within the 30x60 ft spill delineation. Standing water located behind a black tarp at the edge of the delineated area demonstrated normal conductivity (Photos 17-21).-At the time of inspection, SPSI was excavating surficial aggregate/soil that was demonstrating overall conductivity readings of 4 mS/cm (Photos 22-23).-Standing fluid within a sump/trench dug near the left-side of the Kentor Well Site demonstrated normal conductivity (Photos 24-25).Violations of 91.34(A), 78a.57(a), 78a.54, and SWMA 301 are being issued for the spill. In addition, The Department is requesting Leatherwood LLC's Kentor 8H Well plugging secondary containment plan and the maintenance records associated with the secondary containment used in the plugging process.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8278410
Permit API: 123-45905
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Brokenstraw Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/15/2026
Comments: A discharge of production fluids is evident at the Conklin Lease tank battery. Mature trees at the southwest corner of the secondary containment area are either heavily stressed or dead. A brine tank is buried within the secondary containment area. PVC lines connect the drain valves of the stock tanks in containment to cutout holes in the surface of the brine tank. Evidence of previous fluid releases in the containment area are visible via crude oil staining and sawdust sprinkled over the oil-stained areas. It appears that the PVC lines connected to the two stock tanks in the southernmost end of the containment area have been the most heavily used. At the time of this inspection, the PVC lines are placed inside the cutout holes of the brine tank. However, oil-staining, visible wetness, and sawdust sprinkled around these cutout holes indicate that at one time fluid was allowed to run over the surface of the brine tank and onto the ground within the secondary containment area. Elevated specific conductance in soils in excess of 3,000 uS/cm was observed beneath both of the aforementioned PVC lines.A pool of fluid was present in the southernmost end of the containment area, in what appeared to be a sump. At the time of this inspection, the fluid was observed to have elevated specific conductance exceeding 4,000 uS/cm. Soils at the bottom of the sump also had elevated specific conductance which measured in excess of 11,000 uS/cm. The floor of the secondary containment area above the sump was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 uS/cm. A drainage swale is located approximately 30 feet west of the secondary containment area wall. Upslope soil conductivity readings in the swale were observed at 96 uS/cm. Elevated specific conductance in excess of 4,000 uS/cm was observed in soils within the swale directly across from the tank battery. Crude oil staining was also observed in the swale near the tank battery. The swale transitions to an UNT to Irvine Run with defined bed and banks downslope of the tank battery. The water flowing in the UNT was found to have elevated specific conductance exceeding 13,000 uS/cm. Elevated specific conductance of water was observed throughout the stream at the time of this inspection. The specific conductance of water in the stream was observed to drop below 1,000 uS/cm after two confluences with apparently unaffected sources of fresh water at a point approximately 200 feet north of a culvert and the lease road which crosses the UNT. Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with brine disposal receipts for the Conklin lease.

I departed the site at 1130 hours.

Inspection Type: Drilling/Alteration
Inspection Date: 5/02/2023
Comments: On 5/2/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Folta well site. It was 50 degrees and mostly cloudy when I arrived on location. When I arrived on site, I met with Chesapeake's company man, Mack Murry. Mack explained current operations as follows: Precision 573 drilling rig was tripping in the hole with a lateral BHA on the 21HC well. One well has been finished to total depth and after the 21HC there will be two wells left to drill. Six existing wells have been shut in for the duration of the drilling and completion process. Mack expects it to take another 38-40 days to finish drilling at the well site. Mack accompanied me on the site inspection. The drilling rig and all ancillary equipment is staged on secondary containment that is protected by drilling mats. The drill cuttings are collected, solidified, temporarily stored and loaded for disposal; all conducted over secondary containment. Water puddles at the entrance to the drill cuttings area field tested at 0.4 mS conductance or less. Chemicals are stored on secondary containment. The dry chemical additive area is staged on secondary containment. The pathway leading up to the dry chemical additive area is on drilling mats that are not in secondary containment. Water puddles in proximity to the cement unloading area field tested at 0.4 mS conductance. I did witness a rolloff dumpster marked as residual waste at the entrance to the site. The dumpster has a plastic liner but I did witness liquid seeping out of the north west corner of the dumpster and leaving a dark stain in a 12" x 12" area. Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 6/18/2026
Comments: On 6/18/2026, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill (CTS-398645) at the PA Game Commission well pad in Blaine Township, Washington County. The spill reportedly occurred on 6/17/2026 at 8:05 PM, when approximately 20 gallons of produced water/condensate released from a water hauler truck. The Department received the spill report from the operator on the same day at 9:59 PM. The operator reported that the spill was in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1).An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) for this site was terminated on 8/06/2018The following was observed during the inspection:The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection. The reported location of the spill is freshly backfilled with stone, with no residual staining was observed in the remediated area (photo 14). A rolloff box is on site that reportedly contains the impacted material (photo 11). The old GPU/Vertical Separator Units are not equipped with secondary containment (photo 12). However, the associated gas wells were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. The new GPU/Vertical Separator Units are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photo 13). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022. The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) and Safety Data Sheets (SDS) are on site (photos 6 and 7). The ERP appears to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Well 9H is equipped with a well tag (photos 9 and 10). Five additional gas wells are on site that appear to be equipped for production (photo 8). The well and operator's information are displayed and visible on this well tag, as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h). No evidence of a fluid leak, such as staining, was observed on the ground around the gas wells.The well pad and access road appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 2-5).Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being noted and immediately corrected against the 6/17/2026 produced water/condensate release.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.

Comments: This inspection has been conducted in response to an anonymous complaint submitted to the Department on July 29, 2020. The complaint alleged that a poly brine tank, associated with Well #: 019-21522(Haugh 1), was damaged, and has been leaking brine on to the ground surface for some time. These allegations have been verified in the field. A large crack exists on the eastern facing side of the tank. Fluid seems to have drained at a slow but steady rate from above the crack. It is unclear how much fluid has drained from the tank over time. An earthen containment exits around the tank. The leaked fluid, however, seems to be traveling directly down through the soil. It is not clear as to where the fluid is migrating to beyond the contained area. There are no clear outlets in the area immediately beyond the containment. It is recommended that the tank be repaired or replaced to comply with regulatory requirements associated with petroleum brine management and storage.

Comments: On November 26 2024, the Department conducted a routine partial inspection of the Mamont 16 Well Pad (ESCGP-3 issued on 11/30/2021 and expires on 11/29/2026) in regards to a referral from Environmental Protection Specialist (EPS) Zane Shaffer regarding an apparent spill observed outside of secondary containment. Present during today's inspection is Zane Shaffer (DEP) and Justin Ruth (CNX). The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared to be stabilized. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. The Act 9 sign was present at the time of the inspection, and appeared to be in good condition. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, site plans, and Safety Data Sheets (SDS), were present in the onsite mailbox.At the time of the inspection the operator was currently drilling the K well. Mr. Ruth stated the spill outside of secondary containment occurred because an empty barrel of AES WA II (SDS located in the onsite mailbox) was placed inside containment with the valve open therefore residual fluid in the barrel leaked into secondary containment. Then, pipes were accidentally placed on the side of the secondary containment causing a low spot/pinch point to form where the residual fluid mixed with rainwater was able to spill outside of the secondary containment. Mr. Ruth then stated that the pipes were removed off of the containment to stop the spill and all excess water/fluid in containment had been suctioned out.The Department then inspected the area of the apparent spill outside of secondary containment. Upon inspection, a spill was not active, however Zane Shaffer provided a picture of when the spill was active (photo 1). Upon further inspection of the spill, the Department observed orange fluid outside/underneath the secondary containment in the location where the spill had occurred. Conductivity readings were taking in the gravel/soil outside the secondary containment where the spill had occurred and obtained readings of 0.17mS and 0.13mS. A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.14mS.Mr. Ruth stated that they planned to remove the matting and containment and excavate all contaminated gravel/soil and reinstall the containment once complete. He stated they hoped to have all work finished by with in a day or 2. The Department requests clarification on how much fluid was spilled/released outside of the secondary containment with in 2 days of receiving this inspection report.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed spill outside of secondary containment. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending operator response.

Comments: On May 6, 2026, the Department conducted a follow-up inspection to IR 4178322 at the Ritter well site in Redstone Township, Fayette County. Violations were issued in IR 4178322 for failure to conduct long-term maintenance on Post-Construction Stormwater Management Best Management Practices (PCSM BMPs), which appeared to be resulting in accelerated erosion and sedimentation on Tree Farm Road. Tree Farm Road is a township gravel road that connects to the site access road.The Department requested the NOV Response to IR 4178322 from the operator by May 7, 2026. An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) for this site was terminated on July 10, 2017.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of Tree Farm road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in an accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is on site (photo 2). Eight gas wells are onsite that appear to be equipped for production. Well 5H is equipped with a well tag with no observable evidence of a fluid leak to the ground around it (photo 5). The well and operator's information are displayed and visible on this well tag, as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h).The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection. The GPU units are not equipped with secondary containment. However, the gas wells on site were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. No evidence of a fluid leak, such as staining, was observed on the ground around the GPU units (photos 6 and 7).The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 3 and 4). The severe accelerated erosion and sedimentation remains downslope of the well pad on Tree Farm Road (photos 14-24). The Department observed a rock-lined stormwater channel along the access road, which is located upslope of Tree Farm Road. This rock-lined stormwater channel appears to be in need of maintenance, as it appears to be nearly level with the access road (photo 25). Vegetation that appears to be flattened by recent stormwater washout was observed downslope of the rock-lined stormwater channel and at the eastern terminus of the riprap stormwater channel north of the well pad (photos 11-13). The riprap stormwater channel installed north of the well pad is located upslope of the most severely eroded portion of Tree Farm Road. Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued in IR 4178322 shall remain outstanding.

Inspection Date: 2020-03-10
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident response inspection of Repsol's DCNR 594 (02-207) well site located in Bloss and Hamilton Townships, Tioga County on 3/10/2020 at 1225 hours. The weather was 50 degrees with an overcast and rain. Ernie Shumbat represented Repsol onsite and oversaw excavation activities. Bishop Brothers Construction handled the excavation activities and Golder (environmental consultant) handled the environmental side of things. Repsol reported that a water truck had released approximately 20 gallons of produced water from a valve to the pad surface in front of the produced water offload area. The release had impacted the pad material directly in front of the offload area (see photo #3). Golder had tested the pad material for electrical conductivity (EC) and marked the area of impact. While I was onsite, Repsol was still waiting for an 811 call approval for excavation. While awaiting approval, excavation as deep as 12 inches was initiated. Impacted material was scraped up and placed in a lined roll-off container for disposal. Areas after the initial scrape were returned to normal soil EC readings (less than 1.0 mS/cm). The small area directly in front of the offload area (believed to absorb most of the release) was still reading high EC. I left the site around 1340 hours and rain had already began falling. Further excavation was conducted and a reported 7 yards of material was removed from the pad and placed in the roll-off container. Photos were provided by Repsol to show the completed excavation area. The area was backfilled and Repsol was awaiting disposal approval to properly dispose of the impacted material. Due to the observations made during the inspection and the timely response made by the operator, violations of the following were noted as immediately corrected against API # 117-22006: 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 35 P.S. 6018.301 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a)

Comments: On September 28, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow inspection to a reported spill at the Inflection Energy TLC Well Pad. The spill notification was received on September 26, 2021. The DEP met with Inflection Energy Zac Subra found an area of about 50 ft x 80 ft with variable conductivity levels from 1,200 uS/cm to 10,000 u/S/cm. The location of the spill was N 41.3335434, W -76.9287938. Inflection began excavation immediately. Upon arrival, the area of impact had been excavated and backfilled. The spill did not appear to leave the pad surface. The spill was caused by a hole in the containment and a leak in a flushing line used during the well stimulation process. An estimated volume of the leak will be determined when the remainder of the rig mats are removed and the area under the mats can be evaluated. The MASS and freshwater AST still remain on site. This spill causes violations of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. The DEP recommends beginning the Act 2 process when the rig mats are completely removed due to the unknown volume of the spill.

Violation ID: 8240286
Permit API: 129-29266
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland

Inspection Date: 6/30/2025
Comments: On June 30, 2025, the DEP conducted an Incident Inspection of Olympus Energy's Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 6/27/2025 at 2:37 pm.The spill report stated that at 1:15 pm on 6/27/2025, over 5 gallons of a produced water (Photo 12), fresh water, and frack chemicals (Photos 13-15) mixture was released on containment and on the gravel well pad at the Porter Well site.Accompanying during today's inspection is Olympus representative Laura Karosic.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed an Act 9 Sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the DEP observed both an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan, that had all required components.At the time of this inspection, zipper frack operations were being conducted on 2 Utica wells with 57 out of 153 fracks remaining.At the time of this inspection, Ms. Karosic stated that a hose connected to the blender ruptured spraying the mixture on and off containment, however no Waters of the Commonwealth were impacted. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the area of the graveled pad where this incident occurred to be adjacent to a fresh water impoundment located on site. The graveled well pad in this incident appeared to be scraped, the ground in this area was observed to be brown and muddy in comparison to the dry and gray graveled well pad surrounding this area. Ms. Karosic stated that 2-4 inches of the well pad in this incident area was scraped and vacuums were used to suck up any puddles of fluid. The secondary containment where this incident occurred appeared to be clean and dry.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed 3 clamshell dumpsters on site, 2 were full of contaminated material and the 3rd will be filled with any remaining contaminated material once Moody arrives to conduct further remediation efforts.At the time of this inspection, the DEP utilized a conductivity meter to screen the graveled well pad. The DEP collected readings of 8.30 mS, 3.07 mS and 2.20 mS in the incident area and 8.21 mS underneath/at the base of the clean water impoundment. The area outside of this incident area where the ground was not scraped was also screened and the readings collected in that area was comparable to the background reading of 0.333 mS collected in vegetation by the Act 9 Sign. At the time of this inspection, the DEP notified Ms. Karosic of the elevated soil conductivity readings in the incident area and underneath the fresh water impoundment. Ms. Karosic stated that fracking operations is scheduled to commence between July 10-11, 2025, then the fresh water impoundment will be removed and remediation can be conducted in the area where the impoundment was located. The DEP recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(2).At the time of this inspection, Ms. Karosic stated that at this time they estimate that the quantity of the release is between 1 and 3 barrels and that they anticipate following Act 2 protocol for the clean up. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed SDSs for all chemicals on site and included in the release mixture to be located in the on site trailer. Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the 1-3 barrel release of produced water, fresh water, and fracking chemicals on the graveled well pad.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations and how the Operator quantified the amount released. The Operator will need to follow Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) and assess the impacts to the Water of the Commonwealth from the release.

Comments: On 3/10/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an Administrative inspection on the Chesapeake Floydie well site. This inspection is to report the results of two water samples that were collected from water puddles on the south corner and northeast side of the Floydie well site. During an inspection on 1/24/2023, the department discovered high conductance fluid on two areas of the well pad surface outside of containment. In the first area, the fluid covered a 6' x 10' area and field tested at 11.93 mS conductance with an Oakton PCTS-50 meter. The department collected water sample #9551-039 for laboratory analysis from location N 41.665131 W -76.126503. Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
Violation ID: 8242706
Permit API: 129-29266
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/29/2025
Comments: On July 29, 2025, the DEP conducted an Incident Inspection of EQTs Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 7/28/2025 at 2:54 pm.The spill report stated that at 2:06 pm on 7/28/2025, over 5 gallons of production fluids were found on the gravel well pad at the Porter Well site after removing secondary containment. Accompanying during today's inspection is EQTs representative Kyle Borden.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed an Act 9 Sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the DEP observed both an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan, that had different Operator information on it than the Act 9 sign. The DEP recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. At the time of this inspection, drill outs were recently completed on the 6U and containment was removed from the well pad the day prior. Mr. Borden stated that the secondary containment in the release area was packed with tanks and large equipment, therefore despite routine inspections of the containment, only the edges of the containment could be inspected, and no holes or tears were observed. However, upon removal of the containment, staining and small puddles were observed on the gravel pad in an approximately 115 ft x 60 ft area. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the area of the graveled pad where this incident occurred to be adjacent to wellheads covered by boxes. The pea gravel in this area was observed to be wet with sections that appeared to be darker in color than other areas. Mr. Borden stated that SPSI and Moody were arriving on site to remediate the release and that they estimate remediation to be completed within the day. EQT representative Schuyler Brounce mentioned in his email (documented in IR 4024285), that following his review of the incident, he estimates the release to be over 1 barrel. At the time of this inspection, Mr. Borden stated once all contaminated gravel has been removed, an updated quantity will be provided to the DEP.At the time of this inspection, the DEP utilized a conductivity meter to screen the graveled well pad. The DEP collected soil readings of 1.835 mS, 3.22 mS, 3.35 mS and 2.08 mS in the incident area closest to the wellheads, as well as 2.56 mS between two wellheads and a fluid reading of Over Range in fluid observed to be pooled in secondary containment adjacent to the release area. These conductivity readings are elevated when compared to the background soil reading of 0.1457 mS collected in vegetation by the Act 9 Sign.At the time of this inspection, the DEP requested secondary containment logs for the Porter well pad and Mr. Borden stated they would be provided to the Department electronically. The DEP is also requesting an electronic copy of the Safety Data Sheets for all chemicals stored/utilized within and near the secondary containment that was observed to have the release underneath by COB 8/5/2025.The DEP recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(2).Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the over 1 barrel release of production fluids on the graveled well pad.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations and how the Operator quantified the amount released. The Operator will need to follow Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) and assess the impacts to the Water of the Commonwealth from the release.

A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) was entered into between the Department and Diversified on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the Well Site after in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216; after completion of plugging operations.The following was observed during the inspection:A Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the site entrance along Five Forks Road (photos 1 and 2). The Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) control plan available is on site (photos 13-16). An additional RCE is installed where the access road meets the well site, in accordance with the E and S plan drawing (photo 11). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed on site in the locations shown on E and S plan drawing (photos 9, 12, 17, 19, and 20). Some tire rutting was observed in the access road. The tire rutting appears to be severe in the location shown in Photo 7. Due to the soft and damp soil conditions that appear to exist on site, the Department recommends that the operator consider additional E and S control measures as necessary, to prevent accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring on site. Representatives from Next Level Energy were observed staging well plugging equipment during this inspection. No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on site during this inspection. The API number and operator's information are posted on the disconnected meter box at the time of inspection (photo 18). Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being issued against the severe tire rutting in the access road.The Department observed an access road cross-culvert (photo 23). No loose sediment was observed in the cross-culvert during this inspection. However, the Department recommends that the operator take necessary measures to ensure that the cross-culvert is protected from sedimentation. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending re-assessment and re-evaluation of this location in a future inspection.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/02/2023 to PENNECO OIL CO INC in Perry Twp, Fayette county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNECO OIL CO INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/02/2023
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 998052
Permit API: 051-21279
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Perry Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/02/2023
Comments: On June 2 2023, the Department conducted an inspection on the Swiantek 3 OG Well.The findings were as follows: The purpose of this inspection was to respond a brine release that was reported to the Department at 10:00am that occurred on June 2 2023. Penneco stated that there was no release evident during a site visit Monday May 29 2023 but the release was found June 2. No specific time frame on when the release occurred on June 2 is available at this time. The Department is requesting Penneco provide the time at which the release was discovered on June 2, 2023 and by who, to be included in the NOV response. The Department arrived at the well pad at approximately 11:00am.The Department contacted Penneco representative Marc Jacobs via telephone, who proceeded to explain how the spill occurred. Mr. Jacobs explained that shut off valve at the base of the production tank was knocked off. This caused the brine tank to release approximately 30 barrels of brine into the neighboring agricultural field. The Department recommends that the Operator remediate the area in accordance with the Department Spill Policy.The Department also request written clarification from the Operator on how the quantity released was determined by June 14 2023. Soil conductivity readings were taken at the spill site in 5 places throughout the neighboring agricultural field. Soil conductivity readings at the spill site were 7.28mS, 8.18mS, 1.89mS, 6.11mS, and 4.55mS respectively. Visible distressed vegetation extended from base of production tank downslope into agricultural field approximately 158 ft. At the time of the inspection,The well appeared equipped for production. The access road appeared to be stabilized at the time of this inspection. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. The well posting was present at the time of this inspection.Based on today's inspection, violations will be issued. The Department requests that the Operator submit waste manifests when available. The Department will conduct a subsequent inspection to continue to evaluate remediation of this spill.
